newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel to vote on Banerj deal Tuesday. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel to vote on Banerj deal Tuesday. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]

text.p: A much-awaited Senate vote on a deal clearing the way for the privatization of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj is due to take place Tuesday, officials said.

The Senate's Economic Affairs Committee is scheduled to meet at 1000 local/1300 GMT to vote on a request by the Rio de Janeiro state government for approval of a 3.09 billion reais loan to cover Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts.
The loan from federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF), which also has to be approved by the full Senate, is seen as key to make the bank appealing to investors.
Four banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN and Cia de Investimentos Latino-Americana, owned by an unidentified foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual -- have signed up for the auction.
Rio de Janeiro state officials have suggested they would leave to the Central Bank to decide on the future of Banerj if the Senate does not approve the loan.
The Central Bank may liquidate Banerj or extend its special administration of the bank, which expires on June 26, to give the state more time to sell it.

O Globo newspaper Tuesday, quoting an unnamed government source, said the Central Bank would opt to extend its management of Banerj but suggested that the chances for the bank to be sold off are slight.
Banerj is scheduled to be the first Brazilian state-owned bank to be privatized.
It had been scheduled to be privatized last week, but the auction was put on hold pending the Senate approval.
Banerj has been under Central Bank administration since December 1994.
On a day-to-day basis, it has been managed by the private Banco Bozano, Simonsen since January 1996 (corrects from 1995) on behalf of the Central Bank.
Bozano was hired to ready the bank for privatization.
